paragraphs.source_en:
Beauty, written in summer 1816. The earlier poem’s address to the abstraction of
the title, which is perceived not directly but through its various manifestations in
nature, is made at a critical juncture in the poet’s life and leads to a prayer for a
future that will realise a defining moment of insight in youth. This narrative dispo-
sition of present, past and future is shaped in the Ode to the imperatives of autumn
1819. The Hymn’s desire for an ‘onward life’ of autumnal serenity is altered by Ode to
accommodate both a sense of failure and a perception that ‘the price of creativity in
an adult world is destruction’ (Curran (1975) 170). The appeal to the West Wind to
bring about personal dissolution as the condition of creative change S. also recovered
from his own earlier work, in fact from the major poem which was the product. L&C
opens with ‘the rushing of a wind’, agent of a cosmic disruption that is the stimulus
